turns.text: real quick how far am i from holt's number if i get a B in stats. im at a 2.4 rn and need 2.7 for kinesiology

I can work that out. I need two numbers:

1. How many credits you've completed so far (the ones in your 2.4)?
2. How many credits you're taking this semester, and roughly how many each class is worth?

One note: a B in Stats only counts for that class. The 2.7 depends on all your classes this semester together.
about 28 done. this sem is 4 classes 3 credits each so 12. stats is a D after the first two quizzes tho 😮‍💨 just got paid and sent money home so no way im paying for a tutor

Here's the math, with A=4, B=3, C=2, D=1:

- Your 28 credits at 2.4 = 67.2 grade points
- Total after this semester = 40 credits
- 2.7 across 40 credits = 108 points
- You need 40.8 points from this semester's 12 credits, which is a 3.4 semester GPA

If you get a B in Stats (9 points), you need 31.8 from the other 9 credits, about a 3.53 average. That's roughly A-/B+ in each of the other three.

If Stats ends as a C (6 points), the other three need about a 3.87, so basically straight A's. Each letter grade you move Stats up is worth about 3 points, which is the difference between a very hard semester and a nearly impossible one. Stats is the best place to put effort.

The D is only after two quizzes, so it isn't final. Stats grades usually move a lot with homework and exam prep. If it comes up short this semester, the gap carries into spring and you can still close it there.
ok so stats is the rep that matters. i made a weekly study block plan yesterday, 2 hrs stats 3 days a week plus the others. does that math hold up or am i dreaming

The math checks out as a goal. A B in Stats plus roughly B+ to A- in the other three gets you there, and putting the most hours into Stats is the right call. A few things to check in your plan:

- Spread the Stats hours over several days instead of cramming. Practice problems stick better in short, repeated sessions.
- Redo the missed quiz problems first. Those show exactly where you're losing points.
- Don't schedule the blocks right after your shift, when you're too tired to learn anything.

If it's too tight, drop the weaker classes to 1 hour blocks and keep Stats at 2.
fair. free stats help options? short version pls

Short version, all free:

- Your campus tutoring or learning center (most have drop-in stats help)
- Your Stats professor's or TA's office hours, bring your missed quiz problems
- A study group with classmates from the same section
- Khan Academy statistics and Professor Leonard on YouTube for the basics
- The textbook's practice problems with the odd-numbered answers in the back

Start with the tutoring center and office hours this week.
